LESSON: AFRICAN TRADITIONAL EDUCATION

Grade: Grade 5
Subject: SOCIAL STUDIES
Strand: People and Social Organisations
Topic 2.3: African Traditional Education

SECTION 1: WELCOME

Hello! This is a study lesson on African Traditional Education. Read the explanation, follow every worked example, then do the practice. This is original CBC Learn content written from KICD outcomes — not a copy of a commercial textbook.

Big question: How does African traditional education promote values in our community?

SECTION 2: WHAT YOU WILL LEARN

By the end of this lesson, you will be able to:

1. identify methods of instruction used in African traditional education
2. explain the importance of African traditional education in promoting values
3. apply African traditional education in promoting values
4. appreciate the role of African traditional education in promoting values

SECTION 3: STUDY NOTES (READ AND LEARN)

WHAT YOU ARE STUDYING: AFRICAN TRADITIONAL EDUCATION
Subject: SOCIAL STUDIES · Grade: Grade 5
This is a learner study lesson (not a teacher guide). Read every part, follow the models, then practise.

BIG PICTURE
African Traditional Education helps you succeed in SOCIAL STUDIES. You will understand it, practise it, and use it in your county, school, and Kenyan community.

KEY FACTS: AFRICAN TRADITIONAL EDUCATION
Good citizens follow rules, respect others, and care for shared places.
Kenyan examples: lining up, keeping the compound clean, telling the truth, helping a classmate.
Rights come with responsibilities.

PART 1: Identify methods of instruction used in African traditional education

What this means
In this part you learn to identify methods of instruction used in African traditional education. You will use ideas from in your county, school, and Kenyan community.

How to learn it
1. Read the idea carefully: identify methods of instruction used in African traditional education.
2. Locate, explain, then act responsibly using a Kenyan example from your life.
3. Check yourself: Can you explain it without looking?

Model
Locate: Connect “African Traditional Education” to a real place or group in Kenya (school, market, county office, home).

Your turn
Do one short practice that proves you can identify methods of instruction used in African traditional education. Write or say your answer clearly.

PART 2: Explain the importance of African traditional education in promoting values

What this means
In this part you learn to explain the importance of African traditional education in promoting values. You will use ideas from in your county, school, and Kenyan community.

How to learn it
1. Read the idea carefully: explain the importance of African traditional education in promoting values.
2. Locate, explain, then act responsibly using a Kenyan example from your life.
3. Check yourself: Can you explain it without looking?

Model
Explain: Give one cause and one effect linked to African Traditional Education.

Your turn
Do one short practice that proves you can explain the importance of African traditional education in promoting values. Write or say your answer clearly.

PART 3: Apply African traditional education in promoting values

What this means
In this part you learn to apply African traditional education in promoting values. You will use ideas from in your county, school, and Kenyan community.

How to learn it
1. Read the idea carefully: apply African traditional education in promoting values.
2. Locate, explain, then act responsibly using a Kenyan example from your life.
3. Check yourself: Can you explain it without looking?

Model
Participate: Describe one responsible action a Grade learner can take.

Your turn
Do one short practice that proves you can apply African traditional education in promoting values. Write or say your answer clearly.

PART 4: Appreciate the role of African traditional education in promoting values

What this means
In this part you learn to appreciate the role of African traditional education in promoting values. You will use ideas from in your county, school, and Kenyan community.

How to learn it
1. Read the idea carefully: appreciate the role of African traditional education in promoting values.
2. Locate, explain, then act responsibly using a Kenyan example from your life.
3. Check yourself: Can you explain it without looking?

Model
Locate: Connect “African Traditional Education” to a real place or group in Kenya (school, market, county office, home).

Your turn
Do one short practice that proves you can appreciate the role of African traditional education in promoting values. Write or say your answer clearly.

PUT IT TOGETHER
Close your notes and say aloud: what African Traditional Education is, one example, and one way you will practise this week.

SECTION 4: QUICK EXAMPLES

Good citizens follow rules, respect others, and care for shared places.

Kenyan examples: lining up, keeping the compound clean, telling the truth, helping a classmate.

Example 1: Connect “African Traditional Education” to a real place or group in Kenya (school, market, county office, home). (skill: identify methods of instruction used in African traditional education)

Example 2: Give one cause and one effect linked to African Traditional Education. (skill: explain the importance of African traditional education in promoting values)

Example 3: Describe one responsible action a Grade learner can take. (skill: apply African traditional education in promoting values)

Example 4: Connect “African Traditional Education” to a real place or group in Kenya (school, market, county office, home). (skill: appreciate the role of African traditional education in promoting values)

SECTION 5: PRACTICE NOW

1. Write 5 sentences (or show 5 clear steps) that teach African Traditional Education to a classmate.
2. Practise this skill: identify methods of instruction used in African traditional education.
3. Practise this skill: explain the importance of African traditional education in promoting values.
4. Practise this skill: apply African traditional education in promoting values.
5. Make one local Kenya example of African Traditional Education from your county, market, farm, or school.
6. Mark your own work: What did you get right? What will you redo?

SECTION 6: WORK TO DO (HOME / REVISION)

1. In your exercise book, make a one-page revision sheet for African Traditional Education: meaning, 3 examples, 5 practice items.
2. Teach a parent/guardian or younger sibling one part of this lesson (2 minutes).
3. Answer in writing: Why should a Grade 5 learner study African Traditional Education?
4. Prepare for the quiz: cover the Remember box and recite it.

SECTION: THINK ABOUT IT

1. How does African traditional education promote values in our community?

SECTION: REMEMBER

1. Know what African Traditional Education means in your own words.
2. Use local Kenyan examples, not only definitions.
3. Practise in small steps, then check your work.
4. Be able to: identify methods of instruction used in African traditional education.
5. Be able to: explain the importance of African traditional education in promoting values.

Now complete the Revision Quiz. Open Answers only after you finish.

— CBC Learn · Original study notes from KICD outcomes (Strategy 2)
